metadataReview.coordinateBasis: The Agency for Cultural Affairs identifies the present park as the Satsuma position at the top of Sanno-saka. The Japan Tourism Agency independently places the museum on the battlefield. The municipal guide embeds a park/museum locator at latitude 32.91268157959, longitude 130.65159606934, rounded here to four decimals. The archaeological report confirms combat around the adjacent upper road. The modern museum is used only to locate this independently attested battlefield sector; no tactical precision is asserted. Reject the heritage page’s city-hall map centre and the survey abstract’s malformed degree/minute coordinates.

note:
Two opposing formations are identified for Tabaruzaka, 4–20 March 1877. Strengths and losses remain unknown; war-wide troop or death totals are not assigned to this battle. The Satsuma rebels are a local formation, not the abolished domain as a surviving polity. No later Japanese uniform is assigned. Equal symbolic groups and animation timing do not reconstruct tactical proportions or movements.
